newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China on track for record 1996 grain harvest - trade.
newsitem.headline: China on track for record 1996 grain harvest - trade.

text.p: China is on track to meet official projections for total 1996 grain output of a record 475 to 480 million tonnes, traders and diplomats said on Thursday.
"They are now talking about preliminary crop figures of 475-480 million tonnes, which is reasonable," a grain trade executive just returned from a tour of China's northeast said.
"Farmers seem pleased with the crop size," he said. "Everyone is positive about yields, they've had very good weather."
China's official press has said the total grain harvest could reach nearly 480 million tonnes, beating 1995's record output by 15 million tonnes.

A rise early this year in the state purchasing price of cereals had encouraged farmers to grow more grain, the China Daily Business Weekly said last month, quoting officials of the State Statistics Bureau.
China's summer grain harvest was more than 110 million tonnes, up three percent on the 1995 figure.
The early rice harvest hit 44 million tonnes, up 4.2 percent on 1995, the paper said.
Traders expect China's corn crop to be a record 115 to 120 million tonnes, based on increased acreage and increased yields.
Sources who have recently visited the chief corn-growing regions of China told Reuters the crop looks well on target for a harvest of that magnitude.
Heilongjiang province's corn crop should rise from the 12.2 million tonnes harvested in 1995, to between 14 and 15 million, an industry source said.
In Jilin, the corn production should be 17.1 million tonnes, after last year's 14.98 million tonnes, he said.
The increase in land planted for corn was to the detriment of soybeans, trade and industry sources said.
However, they have said soybean yields are expected to improve on 1995, offsetting the acreage fall and ameliorating the reduction in the overall crop.
"Jilin is looking at a total of 680,000 tonnes of soybeans," said the recently travelled source.
"Heilongjiang should be 3.5 to four million. A lot of the trade is saying 3.7 to 3.8 million, which is down from the 4.3 million of 1995," he said.
The total soybean crop is expected to be two to three percent down on 1995's 13 million tonnes, traders said.
Rapeseed output, projected by the state news agency Xinhua to be 8.8 million tonnes, was more likely to be around eight million tonnes, traders said.
The 1995 figure of a record 9.5 million tonnes was an aberration, with 1994's 7.5 million tonnes more in line with the average, one Hong Kong source said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department (USDA) puts China's 1996 total wheat crop at 107 million tonnes, up five million tonnes on the 1995 figure.
With carry-over wheat stocks at 22.7 million tonnes, according to USDA figures, China's 1996/97 (Aug-Sept) wheat imports are expected to be about eight million tonnes.
